newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end up as investors see upside.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end up as investors see upside.

text.p: Caracas stocks rose the second straight session as foreign investors, egged on by a slew of positive research recommendations, took heart in Venezuelan blue chips, traders said.

"Foreign funds continue their interest," said Intervalores broker Ricardo Marino. U.S. Investment bank Morgan Stanley said Monday Venezuelan equities had a 20 percent upside potential for the rest of the year, the highest in the region.
ING Barings, also on Monday, when the bolsa was closed, said investors could still find good buys in services and select consumer and construction stocks.
Telephone company CANTV lead gainers, rising 61 bolivars to end at 2381.00, as the bolsa's 19-share IBC closed up 0.39 percent at 6,611.22 points.
Merinvest's composite index, which includes CANTV, meanwhile gained 0.84 percent to close at 104.35 points.
Among traded stocks, 21 rose, 11 fell and 10 closed flat as 58 million shares exchanged hands, worth 4.6 billion bolivars ($9.5 million).
"I'm sure we'll see further gains this week on continued foreign interest," said Marino.
